chunks: And Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Abū Maryam, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the young goat by which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله passed while it was dead, and he said: “What harm would it have caused its owners had they benefited from its hide?”

Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “It was not dead, O Abū Maryam. Rather, it was emaciated, so its owners slaughtered it and threw it away. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘What would have been upon its owners had they benefited from its hide?’”

key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: an animal dead without valid slaughter; carrion

ai.seo_question: Was the animal mentioned by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله carrion, or had it been slaughtered?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that the animal in question was not carrion, but rather a weakened animal that its owners had slaughtered. It indicates a legal discussion concerning benefiting from the hide of a slaughtered animal and preserves the wording of a statement of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
